key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term photoluminescence degradation of metal halide perovskites from early time-series data, enabling faster stability assessment.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable way to reduce experimental ageing time for perovskite solar-cell materials screening while preserving interpretability.
method: Collected 86k+ PL spectra from 167 perovskite samples under heat and light stress
Featurized spectra with a physics-informed model to capture degradation behavior
Trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM to predict future PL intensity for unseen samples
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on diverse perovskite compositions and crystallinities and was reported to generalize across material groups while outperforming baseline benchmarks.
watch_item: Forecasting performance may depend on how well the training set covers the full range of compositions, crystallinities, and stress conditions seen in deployment.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
